st: Blend the tomatoes, bell peppers, chopped onion and scotch bonnet to a smooth puree.
Pour the puree into a pot and cook uncovered for 15 minutes to reduce and remove the raw tomato taste.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot. Fry the sliced onion for 4 minutes, then the tomato paste for 3 minutes.
Add the puree, curry powder, thyme, bay leaves and [[2 tsp]] salt. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring, until thick and the oil rises to the top.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and drain.
Stir the rice into the sauce and add [[3 cups]] hot broth. It should barely cover the rice.
Cover tightly with foil under the lid. Cook on the lowest heat for 30 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the rice is tender.
Let it rest for 5 minutes, fluff and serve with fried plantain.
Simmer the beef in the broth with half the onion and [[1 tsp]] salt for 35 minutes until tender.
Mix the ground egusi with a little water ([[0.5 cup]]) to make a thick paste.
Heat the palm oil in a large pot. Fry the remaining onion for 3 minutes.
Spoon the egusi paste into the oil in small lumps. Fry for 8 minutes without stirring much, until it forms curds.
Add the beef with its broth, the pepper, crayfish and dried fish. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 4 minutes until wilted.
Season with salt to taste. Serve with pounded yam, fufu or rice.

ing: white yam, peeled and cut in chunks
st: Peel the yam and cut it into chunks about 2 inches big. Rinse well to remove the slime.
Place in a pot with the water and salt. Bring to a boil.
Cook for 20 to 25 minutes until a fork goes in easily.
Drain, keeping a little of the cooking water.
Put the hot yam in a food processor or stand mixer with a dough hook, or pound it in a mortar. Work in batches.
Mix for 3 to 5 minutes, adding a spoonful of the reserved water if needed, until it becomes smooth, stretchy and without lumps.
Shape into smooth balls with a wet spoon. Serve right away with soup such as egusi.
Grind the peanuts in a blender or spice grinder to a coarse powder.
Mix the peanut powder with the cayenne, paprika, ginger, garlic powder, onion powder and salt. This is the suya spice.
Toss the beef strips with the oil and about two-thirds of the spice until well coated.
Marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Thread the beef onto soaked skewers in a zigzag.
Grill or broil on high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Sprinkle with the remaining spice. Serve with the sliced onion and tomato.

ing: or 1 tbsp ground calabash nutmeg and 1 tbsp cayenne
st: Rinse the goat meat and put it in a large pot with the onion, ginger, garlic, nutmeg, [[1 tsp]] salt and the water.
Bring to a boil and skim any foam from the top.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes until the goat is tender. Goat takes a long time.
Stir in the pepper soup spice and the scotch bonnet.
Simmer for 10 more minutes so the broth is fragrant and spicy.
Add the scent leaf or basil and cook 2 minutes more. Season with salt to taste and serve hot in bowls.

ing: soaked 4 hours and skins rubbed off
st: Soak the beans in water for 4 hours. Rub them between your hands to loosen the skins and rinse away the skins.
Blend the peeled beans with the bell pepper, onion, scotch bonnet and the warm water until very smooth.
Stir in the oil, crayfish and [[1.5 tsp]] salt. The batter should be thick but pourable.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, then cool and peel.
Pour the batter into oiled ramekins or foil cups. Press an egg half into each if you like.
Cover each with foil. Place on a rack in a large pot with 2 inches of boiling water.
Steam covered for 50 minutes, adding water as needed, until firm and set in the center.
Cool 5 minutes before unmolding.

ing: soaked 3 hours and skins rubbed off
st: Soak the beans in water for 3 hours, then rub them in your hands to loosen the skins and rinse them off.
Blend the beans, onion, pepper, [[1 tsp]] salt and the water into a thick paste. Add water only a spoon at a time.
Beat the batter with a whisk or wooden spoon for 3 minutes to add air so the fritters turn out fluffy.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Drop in tablespoons of batter, 5 or 6 at a time, taking care not to crowd the pot.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden brown and crisp outside.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with bread or pap.
Stir the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] of the sugar into the warm water and wait 5 minutes until it foams.
Whisk the flour, rest of the sugar, nutmeg and salt in a large bowl.
Pour in the yeast water and stir to a thick, sticky batter. It should be too soft to knead.
Cover and leave in a warm place for 1 hour 15 minutes until doubled and bubbly.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Scoop the dough with a hand or spoon and push balls into the oil. Do not crowd the pot.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning often, until golden brown all over.
Drain on paper towels. Serve warm, plain or dusted with sugar.
Cut both ends off each plantain and slice a line along the skin. Peel it off.
Slice the plantains on a slant into pieces about 1/2 inch thick.
Sprinkle with salt and toss lightly.
Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Fry the slices in a single layer, in batches, for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden brown and caramelized.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

ing: cooked and cubed, plus 1 cup of its broth
st: Simmer the beef in water with a pinch of salt for 35 minutes until tender. Keep [[1 cup]] of the broth.
Blend the bell peppers, scotch bonnet and one onion until smooth.
Cook the puree in a pot for 10 minutes to reduce the liquid.
Heat the palm oil in another pot. Fry the sliced onion for 3 minutes, then the locust beans for 1 minute.
Add the pepper puree and cook for 10 minutes until the oil rises.
Add the beef, broth, crayfish and [[1.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer 5 minutes.
Fold in the spinach and cook just 3 minutes so it stays green. Serve with rice, pounded yam or amala.

ing: cubed, boiled with its broth saved
st: Boil the beef with half the sliced onion and [[1 tsp]] salt for 40 minutes until tender. Keep the broth.
Blend the green peppers, chiles and the onion to a coarse puree.
Cook the puree in a pot, uncovered, for 15 minutes until most of the water is gone. Drain extra liquid.
Heat the palm oil in another pot until it is hot and thin, then reduce heat.
Fry the remaining onion and locust beans for 3 minutes.
Add the cooked pepper puree and fry for 15 minutes, stirring, until the oil separates and the stew turns dark olive green.
Add the beef, [[1 cup]] broth, crayfish and the remaining salt. Simmer 10 minutes. Serve with rice.
Whisk the flour, sugar, nutmeg, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Rub in the cold butter with your fingers until the mix looks like coarse crumbs.
Beat the egg with the milk and pour into the flour. Mix until a firm dough forms.
Knead gently for 2 minutes, then rest the dough, covered, for 15 minutes.
Roll out on a floured counter about 1/4 inch thick. Cut into small squares or strips with a knife.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 340°F (170°C).
Fry in small batches for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until deep golden.
Lift out and drain on paper towels. Let cool completely so it turns crunchy.
Dissolve sugar and yeast in the warm water and wait 8 minutes until foamy.
Add flour, powdered milk, salt and margarine. Mix, then knead hard for 15 minutes until the dough is very smooth and elastic.
Cover and rise in a warm spot for 60 minutes until doubled.
Punch down, shape the dough into a tight oblong loaf and set it in a greased 9 by 5 inch loaf pan.
Cover and proof another 45 minutes until the dough fills the pan.
Bake at 375°F for 35 minutes until deep golden and the base sounds hollow when tapped. Cool before cutting.
nt: Best swap: use whole milk in place of powdered milk and water, swapping 1:1 for the liquid.

st: Rinse the hibiscus under cold water to remove grit, and drain.
Add the hibiscus, [[3 tbsp]] ginger, pineapple and cloves to a pot with [[8 cups]] water. Bring to a boil, then lower to a steady simmer for 25 minutes.
Turn off the heat, cover, and steep until deep ruby red and cooled a bit.
Strain through a fine sieve into a pitcher, stir in [[0.75 cup]] sugar until dissolved, and taste.
Chill thoroughly and serve over ice. It keeps up to 5 days in the fridge.
nt: Best swap: no pineapple, add 1 tbsp lime juice and a little extra sugar; dried hibiscus tea bags (8) work for loose calyces.
